\section{Shared normative authority and notation}
\label{sec:core-notation}

\begin{center}
\fcolorbox{RTCblue}{RTCpale}{\parbox{0.92\linewidth}{
\textbf{Normative core stamp:} \texttt{SCI-RTC-v0.1/r0.10}.  The six files in
\texttt{src/common/} form one authority.  Text outside this shared core is
explanatory or conformance guidance and cannot alter a definition, equation,
assumption, requirement, prediction, unavailable state, or owner decision.
}}
\end{center}

SCI-RTC begins with admitted aligned paired raw detector-coordinate streams
\texttt{xs} and \texttt{rs} and ends with an atomic, consumer-neutral raw
conditioning bundle.  Conditioned $x$ is the required numerical RTC output;
when conditioned $r$ is requested, it is the optional paired companion on
exactly the conditioned-$x$ grid.  The exact paired raw $r$ parent and every
causal $r$ diagnostic or selector remain in that bundle whether or not the
companion is requested.  Conditioned $r$ is neither an independent RTC
pipeline nor a calibrated or Stokes product.  Raw $x$ is not itself a Stokes
parameter.  ALIGN, the Tune/readout mapping authority, AST, and
SCI-BEAM retain authority for the upstream meanings they produce; SCI-CAL may
calibrate only the conditioned $x$ path of an exact RTC bundle.  PTC, VAL,
MAP, BEAM, NOI, MAP-003, FLT, SRC/MODE, and FRUIT retain authority for their
downstream science.  This contract owns the realized conditioning order and
its scientific consequences; it does not infer current software behavior.

The words \ReqWord{shall} and \ReqWord{shall not} identify requirements.
\ReqWord{Required unavailable} means that the affected product or claim shall
not be reported as complete.  \ReqWord{Optional unavailable} is a typed,
scientifically inert state.  Missing, disabled, automatic, rejected, invalid,
failed, unavailable, unsupported, and omitted remain distinct states.

$B^x_\omega$ & Realized post-segmentation $x$-replacement operator conditioned on selection state $\omega$; it has no $r$ numerical branch. \\
$F_{k,\theta_k}$ & Realized ordered FIR, IIR, notch, or admitted mask-controlled stage $k$. \\
$D_{M,0}$ & Integer phase-zero point selector of factor $M\geq1$. \\

\subsection{Identity and interval conventions}

Observation, Tune, array, network/interface, detector occurrence, selected
APT row/binding, native row, aligned slot, scan, science interval, context
interval, conditioned output slot, stage, and product identities are
non-interchangeable.  Array identity is one of \texttt{a1100},
\texttt{a1400}, and \texttt{a2000}; array ID, array index, network ID,
detector index, and container position do not substitute for one another.
Cross-artifact identity requires an explicit occurrence- and product-scoped
binding.  Equal row numbers do not establish identity.

Primary detector timestreams are samples on rows and detectors on columns
unless a product explicitly declares another ordered shape.  Every interval
is half-open.  Science windows, physical scans, processing chunks, filter
context, output selections, and learned-plan scan sets retain separate
identities.  Native, aligned, and output indices never silently renumber one
another.

Time is seconds on the admitted ALIGN-assigned grid.  The approximately
8-ms rate relationships and the $0.5\times$, $2\times$, and $4\times$ family
are conditional software-grid facts, not proof of a detector integration
event, absolute epoch, or astrometric correction.  Coordinate-dependent
Pointing, OOF, and Beammap controls use a declared AltAz tangent plane;
Science controls use a declared equatorial J2000 TAN relation.  RTC performs
no implicit frame conversion.

\subsection{Logical and availability notation}

$\mathbb I[\cdot]$ denotes an indicator, $\E$ expectation, $\Cov$ covariance,
and $\mathrm{supp}(\cdot)$ operator support.  The logical symbols $\land$,
$\lor$, and $\neg$ have their usual meanings.  A quantity decorated
$\Avail$ is present with its required identity, domain, and validity; a
quantity decorated $\Unavail$ is explicitly unavailable.  Neither zero nor
NaN is an availability encoding.

\begin{center}
\textit{End of notation; shared definitions follow without a change of authority.}
\end{center}
